title: The Summer of Port Alder
premise: Dominic Kavanagh inherited Port Alder Vineyards along with its crushing debts, and he plans to sell it to a resort developer by summer's end — until the town's centennial pen-pal program anonymously pairs him with Marisol Vega, the estate manager fighting to keep the vineyard alive. Writing to a stranger, each confesses what they cannot say face-to-face, never suspecting their correspondent is the person they blame for everything. When identities are revealed at the midsummer festival, betrayal collides with tenderness: Dominic must choose between the sale that frees him from his father's shadow and the woman and community that finally feel like home. He tears up the contract, and together they harvest the first profitable vintage in years.
about_author: August Pemberton is the pen name of a former sommelier who traded cellar notes for love stories set in coastal towns. The Summer of Port Alder is the second novel in a planned trilogy about small places and the people stubborn enough to stay.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He arrives at the failing vineyard he inherited, surveys rotting trellises and foreclosure letters, and meets Marisol Vega, who mistakes him for an inspector. Their first exchange is pure friction. Emotional beat: resentment as armor; Dominic resolves to sell and leave by September.

chapters.title: The Centennial Letters
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The town librarian launches a pen-pal program to mark Port Alder's hundredth year, and Marisol signs up on a whim after a brutal day managing a vineyard her late mentor left in her hands. Emotional beat: loneliness admitted only to paper.

chapters.title: A Stranger Named Wren
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Pressured into the program by his aunt, he writes a guarded first letter signed 'Wren.' He vents about a maddening, self-righteous estate manager without naming her. Emotional beat: the strange relief of complaining to no one.

chapters.title: Salt and Second Chances
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She replies to 'Wren,' unburdening about a vineyard's decline and a man she blames for abandoning the land years ago — not knowing Wren is that man's son. Meanwhile Dominic botches a repair she must fix. Emotional beat: kinship forming in the dark.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Remembers
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Inventorying the wine cellar, he finds his father's hidden ledger of debts and a bottle labeled for Marisol's mentor. Guilt surfaces; his letter to Wren grows honest for the first time. Emotional beat: inheritance as wound, not gift.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The resort developer courts Dominic publicly at the marina; Marisol overhears terms that would raze the old vines. She confronts him, and their fight is witnessed by the whole town. Emotional beat: duty hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: Letters We Shouldn't Write
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Both correspondents break the program's one-letter rule, writing twice in a week. Each notices the other feels familiar. A near-miss at the post office almost exposes them. Emotional beat: intimacy outpacing caution.

chapters.title: Fire Season
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A brushfire threatens the north ridge; Dominic and Marisol work side by side through the night wetting down vines. Exhausted, they share whiskey and something softer — then retreat to hostility at dawn. Emotional beat: tenderness glimpsed, then denied.

chapters.title: The Blame in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Her sister arrives, forcing Marisol to admit she stayed in Port Alder out of guilt over her mentor's death, not love. Her next letter confesses she cannot forgive herself. Emotional beat: the enemy she fights is internal.

chapters.title: Contract and Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The developer raises his offer with a deadline: sign before the midsummer festival. Dominic's aunt reveals his father once nearly sold too — and was stopped by Marisol's mentor. Emotional beat: history rhyming, pressure mounting.

chapters.title: Midsummer Festival
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax of Act Two. The librarian reads selected pen-pal letters aloud; phrases both recognize as their own. Eyes meet across the square. Public revelation, public humiliation, Marisol walking into the dark. Emotional beat: betrayal at the moment of truth.

chapters.title: Silence Between Vines
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She stops answering letters and avoids the estate office. Dominic leaves a written apology pinned to her door nightly; she burns none of them but reads all. Emotional beat: anger protecting a bruised heart.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Last Page
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He discovers his father's final entry: a plan to save the vineyard with Marisol's mentor, abandoned out of fear. Dominic realizes he is repeating the pattern. Emotional beat: breaking generational cowardice begins with seeing it.

chapters.title: Rain on the Harvest Road
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. An early storm damages the crush pad days before harvest; crews desert. Dominic appears unasked, working in the rain beside her hired hands. No words, just labor. Emotional beat: actions as apology when words fail.

chapters.title: Wren, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He writes one last letter as Wren — a full confession of identity, fear, and love — and delivers it himself. Marisol refuses to open it. He leaves it anyway. Emotional beat: vulnerability offered without guarantee.

chapters.title: The Unopened Letter
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Alone at night she finally reads it, then rereads every letter, mapping Wren onto the man she's known all along. She weeps for the stranger who knew her best. Emotional beat: forgiveness considered, not yet granted.

chapters.title: Sign Here
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The developer arrives with champagne and contracts. Dominic stalls, asking for one week — through harvest. The developer warns there will be no better offer. Emotional beat: the clock now audible in every scene.

chapters.title: First Crush
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Harvest day: the whole town turns out, found family assembled — aunt, librarian, field hands, Marisol's sister. Dominic and Marisol work in wordless rhythm, and at dusk she finally speaks: 'Tell me why you stayed.' Emotional beat: thaw.

chapters.title: The Night Before Signing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He walks the vineyard at midnight, tasting a grape his father never lived to grow. He drafts two letters — one resigning the sale, one leaving Port Alder forever — and burns neither yet. Emotional beat: choice suspended on a knife edge.

chapters.title: Where the Heart Is a Muscle
chapters.summary: Climax. At the signing, the developer slides the pen across; Dominic instead presents a counterproposal converting debt into a cooperative with the town as shareholders. Marisol stands beside him as witness. The developer walks out; the town holds its breath. Emotional beat: love against duty, duty yielding.

chapters.title: What We Confessed to Strangers
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Weeks later, the librarian publishes the complete correspondence in the centennial anthology. Reading their own letters in public, Dominic and Marisol laugh at how long they took. First kiss in the cellar among the barrels. Emotional beat: joy earned, shyness gone.

chapters.title: The Vintage of Port Alder
chapters.summary: Dual POV epilogue. One year later: the first bottling under the revived Kavanagh-Vega label, the town gathered, Marisol's mentor's reserved bottle finally opened. They write each other one more letter, delivered by hand. Emotional beat: belonging chosen daily; home as verb.
